Became a trader in 6 months  here’s the detailed roadmap I followed ↓”
📍 Month 1 — Master the Fundamentals
Understand how the stock market works, learn candlesticks one by one, study support–resistance, trend basics, NSE/BSE structure, Nifty–BankNifty behaviour, candle psychology, and start watching charts daily for 15–20 minutes without trading.
Goal: Market ki language samajhna.
📍 Month 2 — Price Action Level Up
Learn market structure (HH, HL, LH, LL), premium–discount zones, break of structure, trendline breaks, demand–supply zones. Practice identifying entries on historical charts. Avoid indicators.
Goal: Price kahaan se reverse hoga — predict karna.
📍 Month 3 — Smart Money Concepts (ICT) Foundation
Study liquidity grabs, equal highs/lows, FVG (Fair Value Gaps), order blocks, displacement, inducement, and how institutions trap retail traders. Backtest these concepts on Nifty/BankNifty.
Goal: Market manipulation samajhna — yahi real edge hai.
📍 Month 4 — Build Your Trading System
Pick ONE setup (FVG entry / OB entry / S-R retest). Backtest minimum 100 trades. Learn strict risk management: 1–2% risk, fixed stop loss, no averaging. Understand R:R (Risk–Reward).
Goal: Apna personal profitable setup create karna.
📍 Month 5 — Psychology + Discipline Training
Start journaling every trade. Track emotions (fear, greed, revenge). Remove overtrading. Start meditation/breathing to improve focus. Follow trading rules even when it hurts.
Goal: Mindset → Professional trader mindset.
📍 Month 6 — Consistency & Small-Capital Live Trading
Trade with small quantity, avoid big profits-target, focus on following rules daily. Review weekly results. Remove bad habits. Improve execution. Keep the same setup — no switching.
Goal: Consistency > Profit.

“6 months of intentional learning can change your entire trading career.”

descripcion: If you’re someone who feels like little things make you angrier or irritate you more than they should, I wanted to share 5 practical ways to regulate your anger so you can calm down and respond in a way you feel better afterward.  #angermanagement #emotionalregulation #angercontrol #irritability #copingskills
transcript: How to stop letting little things make you so angry here are five ways from a licensed therapist. No. 1 cool your face. When you're really worked up, go to the bathroom and splash some cold water on your face or play something cool against your cheeks for a little bit. Cooling the face can trigger a parasympathetic response and help slow your heart rate. You're basically giving your body a chance to calm down before deciding how you wanna respond. No. 2 stop assuming the worst in people. Anger gets stronger when you interpret someone's behavior as intentionally disrespectful or malicious. So before deciding this person is so selfish, ask yourself, is there another explanation for what they just did? Maybe they didn't see you. Maybe they just made a mistake. Now, obviously that doesn't mean ignoring harmful behavior or obvious patterns. It just means not adding extra anger to the situation with a story that you don't actually know is true. Number three give your anger a closing time. If something is bothering you, give yourself five or 10 minutes to think about it or write down what you're upset about. Then intentionally shift your attention because repeatedly replaying something in your head is rumination, and rumination tends to keep the anger going. In other words, give the emotion some space without spending the rest of your day rehearsing it. No. 4 lower your arousal before you respond. Take about a minute and breathe really slowly. Try breathing In for about four seconds and breathing out for about six. Research on anger consistently finds that strategies that lower physiological arousal work much better than trying to aggressively get the anger out. So calm your body first, then decide what you actually wanna do. No. 5. Get the basics right. When you're exhausted, your threshold for frustration is going to be much lower.
